lesson_title: One Machine, Two Personalities: Generators and Motors
hook_text: The fan on your desk and the power station feeding it are the SAME machine — running in opposite directions.
clip_script: Here is a secret hiding in plain sight: a motor and a generator are the same machine. Spin the shaft — electricity pours out of the wires. That is every power station on Earth: coal steam, falling water or wind spinning a coil between magnets, and the changing magnetic flux squeezes out a voltage. Now run it backwards: push electricity IN, and the coil gets shoved around by the magnetic field — the shaft spins. That is your fan, your drill, the pump in your fridge. Same copper, same magnets, opposite direction. An electric car does both in the same minute: battery drives the wheels, then braking turns the wheels into a generator and pumps energy back. And the current from a spinning coil comes out naturally sloshing — forward, backward, fifty times a second. That is AC, and the grid chose it on purpose: transformers can pump AC up to sky-high voltage, and high voltage means tiny current, and heat loss goes as current SQUARED — ten times the voltage, one hundred times less waste. The 220 volts at your wall? An honest average of a wave that actually peaks at 311. One machine, two personalities, one clever average — that is the whole topic.
visual_style: A single coil-and-magnet machine flipping between two modes: hands spinning the shaft with lightning flowing out, then lightning flowing in and the shaft spinning; pylons shrinking current arrows as voltage arrows grow; a 220 label riding a wave that peaks at 311.
mood: Revelatory and kinetic — one mechanism unifying the electric world.
pacing: Fast flip between the two personalities, steady beat through the grid argument, crisp rms landing.
